package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of the Spring Core (spring-beans) package allow remote code execution (RCE) via manipulation of the ClassLoader through crafted HTTP POST requests, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable servers running JRE 9+ and Tomcat 9+.

execution_context.file_location: Spring Core (spring-beans) internal request mapping and data binding logic

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: HTTP POST request with crafted parameters that manipulate the ClassLoader, leading to arbitrary code execution via data binding and property access.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes a specially crafted HTTP POST request that manipulates the ClassLoader and data binding mechanisms, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to manipulate internal Java objects and the ClassLoader via external HTTP requests is highly abnormal and dangerous, as it allows attackers to execute arbitrary code remotely.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Spring applications should not allow external HTTP requests to alter internal ClassLoader state or execute arbitrary code. The expected behavior is safe data binding and request handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate use of data binding in Spring is for mapping request parameters to POJOs, not for altering ClassLoader or executing code.
key_indicators: Manipulation of ClassLoader via HTTP parameters
Ability to inject or execute arbitrary code through data binding
Requires JRE 9+ and Tomcat 9+ for exploitability

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP POST request to a vulnerable Spring application.
attack_chain.leads_to: The request is processed by the Spring Core data binding logic.

attack_chain.action: Spring's data binding mechanism interprets the malicious parameters, allowing manipulation of the ClassLoader.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code is loaded and executed on the server (RCE).

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected manipulation of ClassLoader or internal Java objects via HTTP request parameters
Unusual or unauthorized code execution triggered by HTTP POST requests
Abnormal data binding activity leading to class or resource loading
file_indicators: No specific file indicators, as the exploit targets in-memory request handling and data binding logic in Spring Core
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP POST requests with suspicious or non-standard parameters targeting Spring-based endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP POST requests with parameters that attempt to access or modify internal Java classes (e.g., ClassLoader, class.module.classLoader). Look for abnormal data binding activity or stack traces indicating class/resource manipulation. Use updated vulnerability scanners to detect affected Spring Core versions and monitor for unexpected code execution or process spawning in Java applications running on JRE 9+ and Tomcat 9+.
